monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady blanket over the tired wedge I pressed down in the last moment. The air feels thick, like wet paper pressing from a roof I cannot grasp, making the flat shapes I build feel like drawings rather than stone. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the lid above me. I will keep pressing the small rock down on that weary slip, trusting the lean to hold while the memory of a flat anchor fades. The stand feels crowded with forty-three things, and I wonder if the space is real or just a drawing. I need to know if the slip is finally tired enough to stay put or if it will slide off into the dark.
